<reason>B won the decisive comparison: certain subtraction of advertised unpaid posts versus an unproven conversion into paid work. A’s incentive story and “no third honest category” frame were sharp, and A answered pressure questions directly, but A never showed thin-budget roles survive as wages and later named a beneficiary who only gains if they do. B’s public-versus-private-door, exemption dilemma, and stipend-with-conditions alternative stayed live and made the vote easier.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s R1 contradiction (if the working-class never used the unpaid door the ban is pointless; if they did, the ban takes it away), later cashed with A’s concession that the person who can take unpaid weeks is already cushioned.</best_rebuttal>
